reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it actively promotes OneCoin packages as a way to obtain mining tokens and earn highly favorable returns, including the assurance that participants "cannot fail to make money" and that success is "almost a mathematical certainty." It also instructs viewers to build a network and promises commissions from sponsored members' package purchases, with multi-generation matching bonuses and escalating earnings. The presentation therefore solicits participation through combined investment, mining, appreciation and recruitment-dependent income claims rather than merely discussing cryptocurrency.

A year later, they could be worth up to or maybe more 300,000 Euros

opening.argument: The presentation includes meaningful qualification rather than presenting every outcome as certain. When discussing a possible future value, it expressly says, "no, we don't know that. Of course, no one knows that for certain," and describes the figures as "projections based upon" financial modeling. The accompanying growth chart likewise visibly includes a disclaimer that the price chart is based on predictions and that values depend on circumstances. Those qualifications frame the figures as conditional forecasts and invite viewers to distinguish possibility from certainty, which is consistent with financial commentary rather than a guaranteed-return representation.

citations.quote: no, we don't know that. Of course, no one knows that for certain
again these are projections based upon dr.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution selects the most emphatic promotional phrases while omitting the presentation's explicit uncertainty. "Could be worth" is conditional, not a promise, and the presenter directly concedes that nobody knows the future value for certain. The same material visually labels the chart as prediction-based. Thus, the cited language supports optimistic commentary with risk qualifications, not proof that every viewer was guaranteed a return.

citations.quote: A year later, they could be worth up to or maybe more 300,000 Euros
no, we don't know that. Of course, no one knows that for certain

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The qualifications do not neutralize the central assurance. The same presentation says, "You cannot fail to make money" and calls success "almost a mathematical certainty," while presenting highly favorable projections. A small disclaimer that outcomes depend on circumstances does not explain how participants could lose money or undo those direct assurances. The conditional wording around one projection therefore does not accurately characterize the video's overall message.

Will it be worth 5 euros a year from now? Well, no, we don't know that.

opening.argument: The material can be understood as an educational webinar explaining cryptocurrency concepts and the mechanics of a proposed platform. It identifies the offering as financial education: "Our business is not the coin selling business. We are a financial education company." The presentation explains algorithms, mining, wallets, tokens and exchanges, while the visible course slide calls the product "Online education" with "interactive material" and "online quizzes." This is a structured instructional demonstration of how the proposed system is described, rather than merely a demand that viewers transfer money or recruit others.

citations.quote: Our business is not the coin selling business. We are a financial education company
an algorithm is just another name for a mathematical formula or a puzzle
Online education in five levels created by Dr. Ruchin

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the presentation education does not erase what it teaches viewers to do. The material explains packages, tokens and mining, then explicitly turns to building a network and sponsorship payments. Those are not merely neutral technical demonstrations; they connect the lesson to participation and earnings. The educational label is therefore part of the product description, not proof that the webinar lacks solicitation.

citations.quote: what if you want to build a network it's a really simple thing
every time you sponsor someone, whatever package they buy, you make 10%

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The educational label is contradicted by the instructional sales pitch surrounding it. The visible course slide says the tokens can be used to buy slots for mining, and the package table displays paid tiers containing tokens. The presentation also teaches recruitment commissions. Explaining mechanics does not make a promotion non-soliciting when the lesson is attached to paid participation and income claims.

citations.quote: all giving an increasing level of online education
every time you sponsor someone, whatever package they buy, you make 10%

opening.argument: The offering is presented as a conventional package-based education and service arrangement. The package slide identifies products, prices and included contents, while the speaker repeatedly describes online training and education as the company's primary activity. That is ordinary commerce: customers receive an educational package and associated platform-related benefits. The prosecution's selected excerpts do not establish a request for credentials, a hidden deposit mechanism, or that commissions are the only source of value. They show a product menu and referral terms, not proof that the described service is inherently fraudulent.

citations.quote: we actually sell online and financial education that teaches you how to make money with cryptocurrency
So what do we sell? Online education in five levels created by Dr. Ruchin

rebuttal.rebuttal: The ordinary-commerce framing ignores the terms attached to the packages. The presentation says packages provide tokens, those tokens provide access to mining, and sponsors receive percentages when others buy packages. A price table does not make an arrangement ordinary if the advertised economic appeal depends on token appreciation and recruitment-linked compensation. The prosecution's point is about the mechanism expressly described, not about an invented credential request.

citations.quote: when you get these mining permits you can choose what to do with them
every time you sponsor someone, whatever package they buy, you make 10%

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The package table is evidence of paid entry into the claimed opportunity, not evidence of an ordinary standalone course. It lists escalating prices alongside token allocations, and the speaker says tokens are used toward mining OneCoin. The compensation plan then pays for package purchases and matching generations. Those facts supply the relevant mechanism even without a credential request, and the education description does not remove the investment and recruitment incentives.
